metadata.title: Phase H28 Corpus Grammar Omission Quality & Linguistic Defense Audit

Articles (Definite & Indefinite).isl_linguistic_justification: Indian Sign Language has no definite ('the') or indefinite ('a', 'an') articles. Specificity and definiteness are expressed spatially using deictic pointing (IX) or spatial locus establishment, not separate lexical signs.

Copulas & Auxiliary Verbs.isl_linguistic_justification: ISL is a copula-drop language. Predicative adjectives and nominal predicates attach directly to subjects without equative linking verbs (e.g., 'SHE TEACHER', 'HE TIRED'). Auxiliary verbs are expressed by aspectual modulation or modal particles.

Prepositions with Spatial Sign Incorpora.isl_linguistic_justification: Spatial relationships in ISL are conveyed through classifier predicates, direction of verb movement, and spatial loci rather than independent monosyllabic English prepositions.

Discourse Fillers & Spoken Particles.isl_linguistic_justification: Spoken English phonetic pause fillers do not carry semantic content in sign language interpretation and are omitted to avoid cognitive overload and interpretation lag.

Connectives & Conjunctions (Non-manual m.isl_linguistic_justification: Coordination in ISL is signaled via head tilts, body shifts, and prosodic pauses between clause boundaries. Clausal subordination is marked non-manually via brow raise and forward head positioning.
